text:
Molly McCann has spoken honestly about Dana White's recent controversial comments(Image: Reach PLC)

Molly McCann has hit out at Dana White's disparaging comments about men's mental health before the UFC Freedom 250 card at the White House. On Donald Trump's 80th birthday, White will be alongside the President for the fight card taking place on the green lawns of the White House.

The MMA year has seemingly built up to this event, which has been heavily promoted by the US Commander in Chief, who recently suggested the Octagon cage may never be taken down from the prestigious lawn. As White was promoting the event at the back end of May, the UFC CEO suddenly erupted into a rant, stating it's a "weakness" for men to talk about their mental health.

'Meatball Molly' knows White extremely well from her six years and ten months stint in the Octagon. However, she found White's comments unpalatable, particularly considering she and close friend Paddy 'the Baddy' Pimblett heavily promoted men's mental health throughout their time together in the company.

Speaking exclusively to Mirror Sport before her appearance at SoccerAid for Unicef, McCann said: "I feel that’s a soundbite where he’s been frustrated and he’s had enough of people, maybe, being a bit sensitive and soft.

"I think saying men’s mental health is not a real thing when it really is, I think it’s disappointing. He’s quite an advocate for people doing well and looking after people, so it’s quite shocking he said something so polarising.

"It’s a real shame when the stigma of male fighters fighting is that they have to…it’s hard for a man as well in the world. We always say it’s hard to be a woman in this world, but we’re in a place where it’s hard for a man.

"(Sometimes) a man doesn’t know how to be because they keep getting criticised. (They're told) 'You’re too masculine’ or 'You’re too feminine’ or 'You’re too soft.’ You don’t need strong figures saying, ‘Get on with it, man up.’

Trump and White will be centre stage at the White House card

“We’ve had Paddy’s speech, Tyson Fury talking about his mental health. It takes a lot of courage to be honest and be like ‘Hey, I’m on the floor today. You know I’m just letting you know.’ Then to get that response it would be slaughtering. It would do you in a little bit. It’s a shame.”

In July 2022, Pimblett gave one of UFC's most memorable post-match speeches after beating Jordan Leavitt at UFC London. He opened up about his close friend Ricky dying from suicide five hours before the official weigh-in of his bout in the capital.

As part of his speech, the Liverpudlian, who was cheered on ringside by McCann, said: "There's a stigma in this world that men can't talk... I know I'd rather my mate cry on my shoulder than go to his funeral next week. So please, let's get rid of this stigma and, men, start talking."

It's a sharp contrast to White's foul-mouthed rant about men talking about their mental health issues. He made his comments in an interview with Time magazine, where he appeared on the front cover ahead of the White House event.

When the topic was mentioned to him, he said: "Talking about it publicly, I just feel like it opens the door to make young men think that it’s OK to just f***ing go, 'Oh, I’m having mental [health issues] (White says in a whiny voice).

“Handle it behind closed doors. Don’t show that weakness to anybody...I am unapologetically masculine. What is toxic masculinity? Who has it? Who’s too masculine?”
